claim: All 184 independent default case configurations have accepted identical-source results at unchanged bounds across the retained attempts: 28 completed zero-error finite searches and 156 intended replayed counterexamples. Neither full default invocation passed.
grounds: The runner creates a fresh temporary verifier workspace for each case; individual cases share no model state or generated verifier.
Both complete case inventories match all 184 current case signatures in order; the focused retry exactly matches the 21 delegation cases.
All attempts and current files have identical model/runner hashes, limits, model bounds, assumptions and recorded SPIN/compiler versions. No source drift was recorded or detected during review.

Each selected successful case has successful generation and compilation, exact checker flags, and raw search/replay evidence matching its intended result. Expected counterexamples retain matching sources, macro/compiler/run configuration, generated verifier and trail.

The only two incomplete observations are C compilation wall-clock timeouts; neither reached checker execution. Each affected case has a successful unchanged-input observation in another full attempt and the delegation case additionally in the focused retry.

The composer preserves the failed default receipts, selects the latest successful observation for every case, records all raw artifact hashes and states the distinction between case coverage and invocation success. Independent inspection of commands and archives supplements its structural assertions.
limits: This is acceptance of independent named finite-model case obligations, not a successful default command, CI job or single uninterrupted suite invocation.
The evidence does not establish that the full default suite reliably completes under concurrent host load or within an overall timing target.

The individual models retain their declared assumptions and bounds. Casewise conjunction supplies no additional implementation refinement, cross-model composition, cryptographic, detector-quality, deployment or arbitrary-scale guarantee.
Model/runner/case/bound/tool changes require a new source-matched review and affected checks; failures must remain visible rather than be relabelled as passed.
assumptions: One host owner serialises this run and immutable journal writes are atomic
A provider invocation terminates or reaches its fixed external deadline
At most one crash, cancellation or expiry observation; storage survives
An interrupted started external effect is unresolved and not retried; pure handler computation may restart
Deadline values are abstract observations; no wall-clock or scheduling bound is proved
Two disclosure worlds differ only in withheld peer findings
Disclosure applies only to host-managed inputs under the trusted-worker boundary
Provider result values abstract exact parsed JSON; schema and request admissibility are separate inputs
Provider result admission covers one current logical decision, not semantic deduplication across turns
Governed local authority checks are file-snapshot checks, not linearised with later commits or dispatch
Governed replay is an explicit core retry; the A2A service does not automatically resume unknown tasks
Governed representation classes abstract JSON projection, exact HMAC/tenant comparisons and native framing
Privacy response routes and safe event classes abstract the bounded adapter parser and trusted configuration
Notification endpoint acceptance establishes submission only; recipient delivery remains unknown
Privacy response has no automated retry/reconciliation/escalation scheduler or shared case owner
Retained-effect reads use one SQLite snapshot and release it before inspection or authority callbacks
The retained-effect reader performs no recovery, storage writes or worker/effect dispatch
An authorised missing effect is not-recorded; foreign or missing parent and denied reads are unavailable
No unmediated files, provider memory, traffic timing, hash collision or storage adversary
No fairness options, approximate hashing or disabled bounds/assertion checks
This is finite control checking plus implementation correspondence, not a refinement proof
